### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **73** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/migrate-webhook-secrets.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-headers-gate.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-provenance.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b12e16a561cae3da15c09b463b470ce760b11834`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/migrate-webhook-secrets.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-headers-gate.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-provenance.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- **22** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **148** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b12e16a561cae3da15c09b463b470ce760b11834` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cd534ecc718637e49ec42f3365d5b68311df243f` — the merge of head `b4ae8e68332554376921625922f126d6e1e0c09f` into base `b12e16a561cae3da15c09b463b470ce760b11834`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cd534ecc718637e49ec42f3365d5b68311df243f && git checkout cd534ecc718637e49ec42f3365d5b68311df243f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b12e16a561cae3da15c09b463b470ce760b11834 b4ae8e68332554376921625922f126d6e1e0c09f && git checkout -B drift-repro b12e16a561cae3da15c09b463b470ce760b11834 && git merge --no-ff b4ae8e68332554376921625922f126d6e1e0c09f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b12e16a561cae3da15c09b463b470ce760b11834
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b12e16a561cae3da15c09b463b470ce760b11834` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Reviewed by an isolated at-tier reviewer subagent of the adopting seat (`epic:#15194`), read-only: the diff `origin/main...refs/review/pr-24588` (merge-base `5b14b7f3ad8e`), the card, the rulings named below, and the head's check-runs. The head did not move while this was written. Inputs: ruling records 6266750393, 6267391172 and 6270035914 on #15194; ruling 6259141885 on #24435 (Q2 A); the step-0 plan 6268559156 on #24522 (`step_plan.steps[0]`, F1–F6, flags[1]); card #24529 with claim 6267446928 and os-dev-report 6270150096 (no later addendum); PR #24428 as the regime-C pattern; the merged harness.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The seeder retires; D2 becomes true of webhooks — right.** `bootstrap-declared-webhooks.ts` is deleted and `WebhookOutboxPlugin.bootWebhookTable` (webhook-outbox-plugin.ts:315-341) binds one `DeclaredWebhookSource` as the `declaredWebhooks` service on the data engine alone, before `bootAutoEnqueue`, so the activation door answers on a kernel that dispatches nothing. The read order is the seeder's (`_registry.listItems('webhook')`, then the metadata service, a promise not awaited — `readDeclaredWebhookItems`, declared-webhooks.ts:133); both `_registry` and `registry` resolve on `ObjectQL` (engine.ts:4688, :4725). Pinned: the plugin boot records zero `sys_webhook` writes (declared-webhooks.test.ts, "nothing writes a sys_webhook row"); the ADR-0054 proof boots the real stack without realtime and asserts no row, the bound reader, and a dispatch with `object`→`object_name` applied.
2. **Fresh install dispatch — right.** `projectDeclared` (auto-enqueuer.ts:611) runs the declaration through `parseRow`, so the trigger drift-guard and `webhook/without-triggers` apply as to a row; `secret` and `headers` are lifted off the parsed declaration into the cached subscription and never stored; the subscription id and every delivery's `ref_id` are `declared:NAME`. A declared webhook signs byte-identically with no row, no cipher and no CryptoProvider (webhook-secret-at-rest.test.ts, the two new pins). An invalid declaration is skipped with one warning per name; the first registration of a name holds it, as the seeder's upsert did.
3. **The organization dimension — right, and it is what the plan's constraint meant.** Measured on `main`: the 18.0 mirror is stamped with the Default Organization (fixture row `org_mvf8cxynmka5sb9b`) and its two deliveries with the same. Step 0's constraint "serve in the Default Organization under `single`" is met by `deploymentWide` (auto-enqueuer.ts:581-598, :1204, :1351, :1432): under a posture with no wall the declaration receives every organization's events and each delivery is stamped with the EVENT's organization, which under `single` is the Default Organization (D9). Under a wall the 2026-09-07 org-less refusal stands, said once; an absent or unreadable `tenancy` service reads as walled (`postureBuildsNoWall`, webhook-outbox-plugin.ts:488). Pinned three ways, posture read included.
4. **The 18.0 dual read — right on all three constraints.** `classifyDeclaredNameHolder` (declared-webhooks.ts:253) reproduces the 18.0 seeder's own treatment of a row holding a declared name: a pristine `package` mirror is skipped in `doRefresh` (auto-enqueuer.ts:485, `mirrorIds`) and the declaration answers — one delivery, never two, following the declaration's URL and switch, exactly as the seeder's rewrite on every boot made it do; a `customized: true` row or an `admin` row answers as itself and the declaration is withheld with one `warn` per name per process carrying the remedy, so an administrator's `active: false` keeps holding; a mirror whose declaration is gone keeps dispatching. No code path moves or deletes an 18.0 row: the fixture's seven dual-read pins assert `engine.writes` empty, and the only remaining boot write is the pre-existing cleartext sweep. The committed harness fixture's row is `customized: 1, active: 1` under a declaration shipped `isActive: false` — the "row" branch, pinned by "a seeded row an administrator pointed elsewhere (customized) answers as itself"; the harness itself is unmeasured on this head (③ item 2).
5. **The redelivery veto — right.** A `declared:` ref is judged by the declaration (not declared any more → refused; switched off → refused); a row id is judged by the row; a pristine mirror still declared is judged by its declaration, a customized one by the row (redeliver-guard.ts:124-126, :143; `judgeDeclared` :200). A lookup that throws propagates: "could not check" never reads as "allowed". Four pins, the pristine-mirror replay included.
6. **The regime-C switch — right, in both directions.** `active: switched.get(name) ?? webhook.isActive !== false` (declared-webhooks.ts:173; the ledger read `readWebhookActivation` :217): a ledger row of type `webhook` overrides the declared `isActive` either way, another type's row of the same name does nothing, a composition without the ledger object issues no read, and a failed read keeps the declared default for that pass with a `warn` — the sharing-rule reader's conservative rule. A ledger write refreshes the cache in the same request through a third realtime subscription on `sys_metadata_activation` (auto-enqueuer.ts:382-384, `handleLedgerEvent` :1491); #24428 used a data hook, but this plugin already refreshes its `sys_webhook` cache through realtime, dispatch needs realtime anyway, and the shutdown pin now counts three subscriptions released. Five pins.
7. **The door — right, with `sharing_rule` preserved.** `webhook` is admitted beside `sharing_rule` through one `DECLARATION_LOOKUPS` table (catalog-activation.ts:91, :144-174); the two tiers are unchanged (`manage_metadata`, then the ADR-0126 §5 posture rule — the platform operator under `group`/`isolated`, `WEBHOOK_ACTIVATION_SUBJECT` wording in activation-gate.ts:201); 404 for an undeclared name, 503 when no reader is bound or the read fails (a reader that throws before its promise is a failed read, :295), the package recorded, a package-less declaration admitted. Seven pins; the six `sharing_rule` pins stay green with the generalised messages.
8. **R1–R4 — right; nothing walled-only or posture-dependent beyond the rulings.** R1 measured on a fresh showcase (0 rows; door 200/404; one `declared:` delivery; switched off, none). R3 untouched. R4: `serve.ts` untouched; the only posture-dependent branch is `deploymentWide`, taken only where the posture builds no wall. The walled shape of a declared webhook is deferred to step 4 (③ item 6).
9. **Complete feature (6270035914) — right for the API contract.** A new install writes the new shape and dispatches it; the switch works through the door; the 18.0 shape is still read. Nothing is dormant. The console counterpart is owed separately (③ item 7).
10. **The liveness ledger — the measured verdict is right; its consequence is not carried through the tree (blocking, see verdict).** `packages/spec/liveness/webhook.json` re-anchors nine props to the registry read and flips `label` and `description` to `dead` (their only reader was the seeded Setup row). `dead` is a ruled verdict that warns an author with no opt-in (lint-liveness-properties.ts:169-176, :261-265: "has no runtime effect (liveness: dead) … Remove it"). The PR's own tree contradicts that: `packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.test.ts:258-271` pins ZERO findings for an authored `description` against the REAL `webhook.json`, and `examples/app-showcase/src/automation/webhooks/index.ts` still authors `label` and `description`. This is what reddened `Test Core (2/6)` (the shard's annotation: `packages/lint` `pnpm run test` exited 1; `main` is green on that shard at `ec16dbe2` and `5a871e4e`). The dev's 178 gate commands do not include the lint package's unit tests, and `check:liveness` judges only the ledger's internal consistency.
11. **Spec, docs and ledgers — right.** `webhook.zod.ts` and the retired-keys entry change doc comments only (no schema change; `WebhookSchema` still admits the envelope keys the registry stamps). The tenant-audit census was regenerated with the tool (231→229: the seeder's two writes); the four `scripts/*` baselines are re-keyed for the renamed test or shrunk for the deleted source; the showcase docblock names the door. Left unchanged, rightly: `organization-ownership-inventory.ts:548-555` (turning `declared` into a `mirror-deletion` departure is ceremony behaviour), `sys-metadata-activation.object.ts`, `serve.ts`, every #24522 harness file, `docs/adr/**`, `content/docs/releases/`.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and in `.changeset/24529-declared-webhooks-from-registry.md` — the right arm. `yes`: the diff adds accepted surface on published payloads (`:type = webhook` on `POST /api/v1/security/_activation/:type/:name`, `metadata_type = webhook` rows in `sys_metadata_activation`, `ref_id = declared:NAME` on `sys_http_delivery`). `(narrowing)`: the editable Setup row for a declared webhook, the `customized: true` path, is gone — BREAKING, shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention (`check-changeset-no-major` refuses a `major`). Levels: `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks` minor and `@objectstack/runtime` minor (both move published source), `@objectstack/spec` patch (doc comments and the shipped liveness ledger; no schema key added, removed or renamed). The ADR-0087 marker is `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, the disposition #24428 carried and the right one here: no authorable key, export, option or stored shape is added, removed or renamed; the 18.0 rows stay in place and keep reading. The FROM→TO is stated (editable seeded row → the activation door for the switch plus a copy under a new name for a change; `managed_by: 'package'` row → none). No public export is removed: `src/index.ts` is untouched, and `bootstrapDeclaredWebhooks`, `headersPatch` (webhook-headers.ts) and `canResolveSecrets` (webhook-secret.ts) were module-level only. `Check Changeset` is green on this head. If the fix for the blocking item retires `label`/`description` from `WebhookSchema` rather than from the showcase alone, that is a schema face and a spec `minor` with a tombstone — not this PR.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Gate state on this head** (40 of 41 check-runs concluded at write): `Test Core (2/6)` FAILURE — `packages/lint` tests, PR-caused (① item 10); `Test Core (3/6)` success (it was still running at dispatch); the aggregate `Test Core` in progress; everything else green; `Dogfood Regression Gate (n/3)`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Console Pin Gate` and `Temporal Conformance` skipped by `ci.yml:2026` on `pull_request`. The shard log tail (job 118128990150) shows the cli package green; the lint failure is above the 400-line tail and is read here from the annotation plus the test source.
2. **Merge gate (6267391172 item 3) not yet met on this head.** The harness merged at `ec16dbe2` (PR #24552, 14:45Z); it is not an ancestor of `6b3042a8` (merge-base `5b14b7f3`, nine commits behind `origin/main`), so the head does not contain `upgrade-18x-harness.dogfood.test.ts` and R2 is unmeasured here. The dogfood job never runs on `pull_request`, and the opt-in lane (PR #24554) is open and Tier H — so "harness green" can only come from the lane or a run the seat makes. The next head must merge `origin/main` and show the harness green before its landing record. Step 0's pr_cut asked the step-1 PR to add one harness case (the customized mirror dispatches exactly once); the claim's surface forbids touching #24522's harness files, and the dev followed the claim — the equivalent shape is pinned in `declared-webhooks.test.ts` only.
3. **`ceremony_owes` (6270150096) — complete for the tables, two precisions owed before step 5.** Covered: pristine-mirror deletion and the `mirror-deletion` departure on inventory :548-555; customized-row settlement; `sys_http_delivery` re-source; orphaned `sys_secret` ciphers; the `customized` / `managed_by` columns; the step-7 code (dual read, provenance stamp, sweep's package half). Owed: (a) owes[1] settles every customized row as "a copy under a new name plus the declaration switched off", but step 0's `ceremony_must_later` distinguishes an `active`-only customization (an activation row, no clone) from any other edit (a clone plus the switch) — the committed fixture's row (`active: 1` under `isActive: false`, URL unchanged) is the `active`-only case; (b) owes[3] re-sources deleted mirrors' tails to `declared:NAME`, which is right for pristine mirrors only — a customized mirror converted to a clone must have its tail re-sourced to the clone's row id. The ceremony's anchor walk (organization-ownership-plan.ts:1171-1201) touches only `organization_id IS NULL` rows, and a `declared:` delivery is always stamped, so the `parent('ref_id','sys_webhook')` anchor owes nothing.
4. **The 409 name guard — not required for this step; required before step 4.** Answer to the open question: under `single` the only actor who can author a `sys_webhook` row under a declared name is the same administrator the door serves, the withhold is warned once with the remedy, and no 18.0 data is at risk, so the omission does not block step 1. But `heldByRow` (auto-enqueuer.ts:575-590) is deployment-global by name: once a wall exists (step 4), one organization's same-name row would silence a deployment-wide declaration for every organization — the cross-organization effect `bindDeclaredRuleNameGuard` (sharing-rule-service.ts:237) exists to refuse, and part of "the shape #24378 ruled A" that 6259141885 cites. Carry it to the step-4 card (#24580) or its own card: refuse an insert of a declared name and a rename onto one with 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, system writes and the existing 18.0 rows untouched — compatible with expand-first. "Expand-first adds no new refusal" is not what 6266750393 item 2 says; it governs data moves and deletes.
5. **Prose/code mismatch on `platform` rows.** The PR body and owes[0] say pristine mirrors are `managed_by` in `package`/`platform`; `classifyDeclaredNameHolder` treats only `package` as a mirror, while the 18.0 seeder overwrote every row that was neither `admin` nor `customized`. Harmless for seeder-written rows (always `package`); align the predicate or the prose at step 5/7.
6. **Walled posture is deferred, rightly, but step 4 must decide it.** Under a wall a declared webhook is org-less and refused with one warning — unreachable while R4 refuses walled boots. The step-4 card must choose the walled shape (deployment-wide across the wall, or per-organization) consistent with 6259141885's rejection of Q2 C (silent loss under a wall).
7. **Console counterpart owed.** Setup → Integrations → Webhooks no longer lists declared webhooks and nothing in the console switches one; the API door is the only switch. The objectui "Disable and Clone" surface (as #12982 for sharing rules) is a card of its own. The enforce-or-remove debt on `label` / `description` (ADR-0049) is that card's input.
8. **Checklist text contradicts the measured behaviour.** `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/integration-system.json` revision 8 still says the declaration "is read ORG-LESS … so it delivers nothing on the org-walled showcase" (fixtures.requires[0], steps[1]); commit `723af9722` made it deployment-wide under `single`, and the PR's own fresh showcase boot recorded one `declared:` delivery stamped with the Default Organization. Fix the two strings; `AutoEnqueuer.admitsOrganization`'s docblock is stale the same way (the dev noted it).
9. **Out-of-surface edits — accepted** (`packages/spec` liveness and comments, `packages/qa/dogfood` webhook proof and fixture, the checklist item, `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`, the regenerated census, the showcase docblock, four `scripts/*` ledgers): each is a consequence of deleting the seeder; none is a #24522 harness file, an ADR or a releases page.
10. **Size.** 1,869 + 1,129 = 2,998 lines against the 3,000 cap (6270035914 item 2); `Check PR Size` green. The fix for the blocking item must stay within two lines net, or the landing becomes Tier H.

Blocking item, with its fix:

- **B1 — the `dead` flip of `label` / `description` is not carried through the tree, and the head is red on it.** `packages/spec/liveness/webhook.json` (`label`, `description`: `status: "dead"`) vs `packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.test.ts:258-271` (pins zero findings for an authored `description` against the real ledger) and `examples/app-showcase/src/automation/webhooks/index.ts:21,27` (authors `label` and `description`, which `objectstack lint` now tells its author to remove). Fix, keeping the measured verdict: update the regression guard at `lint-liveness-properties.test.ts:258-271` to expect the `liveness-dead-property` finding for `description` (and `label`, if authored) with the ledger's note as its hint, and drop `label` and `description` from the showcase declaration so the shipped example does not warn; then run `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test` and let `Test Core (2/6)` go green. The alternative — grading the two rows `planned` — is honest only once a card commits to the Setup surface that would read them, so it is not the fix for this head.

## Seat re-review · `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (B1 only) · epic PM `session_01Y5583bs2RDd53MH6kM1ca3` (`os-steve`) · 2026-10-19T17:04Z

Head `9bce0aaf`. This supersedes the FAIL of 6271423990 on its single blocking item. Every other judgment in that record stands.

- **B1 resolved.**
  - The two `dead` liveness rows (`label`, `description`) gain an `authorHint`.
  - The guard at `lint-liveness-properties.test.ts` now expects exactly those two `liveness-dead-property` findings, with that hint. A new case pins silence for a declaration that authors only what is delivered on.
  - The showcase declaration drops both keys.
  - Lint: 148 files, 6,924 passed (addendum 6271777060).
- **The merge gate is met.** `origin/main` is merged (`5a871e4e`, which carries the harness). The harness passes 6/6, including the new case 2b: the 18.0 customized declared webhook dispatches exactly once on a task change. Ablation turned 2b red, and the restore was proven.
- **CI on `9bce0aaf`:** 36 success, 5 skipped, 0 failed.
- The two checklist strings and the `admitsOrganization` docblock were fixed in the same push.
